title: Fatal Dance
transcript: Rook to H7. White is a genius and he's trying to cut out the black king from the rest of the board. Of course, now coming to a fate wouldn't make any sense because this check would win the queen. So, the king goes to D8. And it seems like black is pretty much safe. The black queen should be enough to fend off two rooks. They are about worth the same. But white continues with rook to A6, now threatening a ladder checkmate with the two [music] rooks. Black cannot allow that. So, he has to try to give checks to the white king. But, surprisingly, this is not very easy. None of these checks are safe. This one is covered by the rook. So, the queen has to give a check on F8. The king is completely wide open, so he has to tread very carefully. And the only [music] move that continues the attack is king to G3. Now again, pretty much every check is covered except for queen to G8 check, which seems to just allow a complete fork of the king and rook. Are we going to lose a rook? Well, not exactly. After the brilliant king to F2, just leaving the rook to hang, we realize that the black queen actually cannot take this rook because of the very precise rook to A8 check. The king has to move [music] off the last rank and after the rook to A7 check, we are going to pick up the queen. So, black has to keep checking the white king. But again, the only safe check available is queen to F8 check. But black realizes that if he decides to go down this route, actually, the white king is going to walk away and eventually reach the D2 square from where there is not going to be a single safe check with this black queen. And the queen cannot keep going this way because her own king is in the way. So, instead of that, black has to try and stop the checkmate threat on A8. So, he plays queen to D5. Now, the checkmate threat is stopped, and if you give a check this way, the black king is simply going to be able to walk away. So, it seems like black is simply out of the woods, and this is going to be a draw, right? Well, not exactly. Unfortunately, queen to D5 does not stop rook to A8 whatsoever. This is a brilliant sacrifice, but with a pretty simple idea. Of course, the rook has to be taken, but now the black king and the black queen are perfectly lined up, and rook to H8 [music] is going to pick up the queen and win the game.
